If sentiment is consistently high (≥0.67) in the last 3 days, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% for early horizon (1–7 days) to avoid over-optimism.

If sentiment is consistently low (≤0.33) in the last 3 days, increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% for mid horizon (8–15 days) to counteract pessimism.

If sentiment spikes to 1.00 in the last 2 days, shift forecast upward by 1–2% for late horizon (16–30 days) to capture momentum.

If sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67) and forecast is trending upward, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% for mid horizon to prevent overcorrection.

If sentiment is mixed and forecast is trending downward, increase forecast by 0.5–1.0% for early horizon to avoid premature sell-off.

If sentiment is uniformly low across 5+ days, apply a 1.5–2.0% downward bias to all horizon segments to reflect structural bearishness.
